units.meaning: If an employer fails to maintain an accurate record of an employee's hours worked—including for employees exempt from the FLSA hours-worked recordkeeping requirement (such as bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees under 29 CFR part 541)—the employer bears the burden of establishing that the employee did not work the required hours of service.

source_spans.quote: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's requirement that a record be kept of their hours worked (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees as defined in FLSA Regulations, 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours.

units.meaning: When accurate hours-worked records are not maintained, an employer wishing to assert that full-time teachers (defined in § 825.102) of an elementary or secondary school system, higher education institution, or other educational establishment or institution are ineligible for FMLA leave must clearly demonstrate that the teachers did not work at least 1,250 hours during the preceding 12 months, taking into account that such teachers often work outside the classroom or at home.

source_spans.quote: An employer must be able to clearly demonstrate, for example, that full-time teachers ( see § 825.102 for definition) of an elementary or secondary school system, or institution of higher education, or other educational establishment or institution (who often work outside the classroom or at their homes) did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the teachers are not eligible for FMLA leave.

In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's requirement that a record be kept of their hours worked (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees as defined in FLSA Regulations, 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours.

units.meaning: Provides a cross-reference directing to § 825.801(d) for specialized rules governing airline flight crew employees, without establishing an independent substantive requirement within this subsection.

source_spans.quote: See § 825.801(d) for special rules applicable to airline flight crew employees.
